version.source_text:
Preparation of a 2% Saline Solution
Teaching-lab practice protocol for testing LabJarvis. Uses only water and table salt; it is not a validated laboratory procedure.
Materials
• Distilled water (at least 100 mL)
• Sodium chloride (table salt)
• 70% ethanol for wiping the bench
• 250 mL beaker, spoon or stirring rod, kitchen scale, thermometer
Procedure
1. Wipe the bench with 70% ethanol and let it dry for 1 minute.
2. Add 100 mL distilled water to a clean 250 mL beaker.
3. Add 2 g sodium chloride to the water.
Caution: do not taste the solution and keep it away from food.
4. Stir the solution for 2 minutes.
5. Measure the temperature of the solution with the thermometer and record it.
6. Leave the beaker to settle for 3 minutes.
7. Record an observation describing whether the solution is clear or cloudy.
8. Label the beaker with the date and your initials and store it at room temperature.
Notes
The expected result is a clear, colourless solution. Dispose of it down the sink with plenty of water.
